analysis:
The only production change is SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry (head lines 1771-1780). It now returns 0 immediately if the cache is closed. Otherwise it delegates the victim walk to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:isClosed:), which receives an isClosed closure and a per-tag retire callback. The callback still goes through retireIndexedEntries (lines 1786-1796). That path takes removalLock and requires hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot, which checks !closed and the current epoch, and then calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove with root and epochStore. The delegation therefore adds no new file-deletion authority. The root-safety, symlink-safe removal and epoch-ownership checks (T-041 posture) remain on the deletion path. The closed-store early exit removes a loop that previously revisited every candidate after close, so it narrows work and adds no exposure. Stats are updated only when bytes were freed.

The previous code returned 0 when retired.externalChange was set. The new helper's handling of externalChange lives in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement and the new SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot, which are outside the supplied units. The test changes call oldestFirstSnapshot and rely on lazy snapshot ordering that I could not inspect. I could not verify that the helper preserves the previous behavior: a leased or busy file is skipped without deletion, an external change aborts the pass, and the walk is bounded. The test code in SSDClosedStoreEvictionTests and SSDBlockIndexTests is test-only and has no production security impact. It creates plain fixtures in temp directories and uses a spawned thread.

No regression is evident in the supplied lines. Remaining question for integration: confirm SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest and SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot are bounded, race-safe against concurrent index mutation, and do not delete outside the model root.
